Week in brief

Agent ID service plans are slated for July, while Authenticator’s rooted-device block is the clearest behavior change

The week of 15 June 2026 was primarily documentation maintenance: 3,010 update records, seven new records, and no removals. The two Message Center notices carry the strongest operational signals—a July 2026 rollout of Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents, and a warning-then-blocking Authenticator change for Entra credentials on jailbroken or rooted mobile devices. The Learn material otherwise points to scoped migration, preview, developer, and tutorial guidance; it does not establish a broad GA or retirement. For example, the Internet Access update simply clarifies that later labs should reuse the baseline security profile and Conditional Access policy.

  • Security Copilot · Conditional Access
    Agent ID service plans are announced for a July 2026 rollout

    A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says Microsoft is adding Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents to Microsoft Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 E7, with rollout starting in July 2026. The notice describes automatic enabling and no policy changes, while recommending a license review. Related Agent ID documentation covers OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, sidecar and federation patterns, and Conditional Access evaluation of on-behalf-of token exchanges; those Learn edits provide implementation context rather14.4

  • Entra ID · Authentication
    Authenticator’s rooted- or jailbroken-device credential blocking is an automatic security behavior change

    A separate Message Center notice describes a phased Microsoft Authenticator rollout that it dates from February 2026: users first receive warnings, followed by blocking of Entra credentials on jailbroken or rooted iOS and Android devices. It says the behavior is automatic and affects all users on such devices, with no admin action required, but asks administrators to notify users and update documentation. The evidence does not describe this as a new Conditional Access control.

  • ID Protection · Architecture
    ROPC guidance reiterates deprecation without announcing a retirement date

    The updated Entra ID article for desktop applications explains that the username-and-password, or ROPC, flow is deprecated, why it is discouraged, and how to move to more secure authentication flows. This is security and migration guidance, not evidence that ROPC was removed or that enforcement changed this week. No retirement deadline is supplied.

  • Workload ID · Security
    Workload ID documents SAP SuccessFactors provisioning with federated OIDC tokens in Preview

    The updated Workload ID article is explicitly marked Preview and describes replacing basic authentication for Microsoft Entra provisioning to SAP SuccessFactors with short-lived, federated OpenID Connect tokens. The scope is the SAP SuccessFactors provisioning scenario; the record does not establish general availability or a tenant-wide authentication change. Administrators using that integration can assess the preview, while no broader action is indicated.

  • Global Secure Access · Fundamentals
    Global Secure Access and External ID updates are scoped implementation guidance

    Global Secure Access documentation was updated for configuring a Conditional Access policy for Explicit Forward Proxy, and the title labels the capability Preview. Separately, a new External ID article shows Android (Kotlin) developers how to attach custom x-* headers to native authentication requests for fraud-detection SDK integration. These are scenario-specific Learn changes, not evidence of GA, a tenant-wide behavior change, or required administrator configuration.

For Entra administrators

Review licensing for the two Agent ID service plans, as Microsoft recommends, but the notice says no policy changes or immediate action are required. Notify users about the Authenticator behavior and update internal documentation. Organizations using desktop apps with ROPC should consult the migration guidance, while SAP SuccessFactors provisioning customers can assess the Workload ID preview. The External ID and Global Secure Access entries are scenario-specific documentation and do not evidence a required tenant-wide change.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.

Licensing Authentication

Updated

The following table lists features that are available for authentication in the various versions of Microsoft Entra ID. Plan out your needs for securing user sign-in, then determine which approach meets those requirements. For example, although Microsoft Entra ID Free provides security defaults with multifactor authentication, only Microsoft Authenticator can be used for the authentication prompt, including text and voice calls. This approach might be a limitation if you can't make sure that Authenticator is installed on a user's personal device.

19 June 2026

Microsoft Authenticator app: Upcoming changes to jailbreak and root detection

New

Starting February 2026, Microsoft Authenticator will block Entra credentials on jailbroken/rooted iOS and Android devices to enhance security. The rollout includes a warning phase followed by blocking. This feature is automatic, affects all users on such devices, and requires no admin action. Notify users and update documentation accordingly.

Entitlement Management Access Package Manage Lifecycle

Updated

Guest users that already existed in your tenant by being invited are ungoverned. After an ungoverned guest that requests access packages lose their last access package assignment, they'll remain in the tenant indefinitely. If there are guests that have an access package assignment, and only need access from that access package, and there's no other need for them to remain in the tenant, you can convert them to be governed during the time they have that access package assignment. You can directly convert those ungoverned users to be governed by using the **Mark Guests as Governed** functionality in the top menu bar of an access package.

Faq Customers

Microsoft Entra External ID pricing is based on monthly active users (MAU), which is the count of unique users with authentication activity within a calendar month. Multifactor Authentication Customers

Updated

18 June 2026

Authentication Methods Customers

Updated

With Microsoft Entra External ID, you can create secure, customized sign-in experiences for your consumer- and business customer-facing apps. In an external tenant, there are several ways for users to sign up for your app. They can create an account using their email and either a password or a one-time passcode. Or, if you enable sign-in with Facebook, Google, Apple, a Microsoft Entra ID tenant, or a custom OIDC or SAML/WS-Fed identity provider (IdP), users can sign in using their credentials in the external identity provider. A user object is created for them in your directory with the identity information collected during sign-up.

18 June 2026

Custom Extensions

Updated

Microsoft Entra External ID user flows are designed for flexibility. Within a sign-up and sign-in user flow, there are built-in authentication events. You can also add custom authentication extensions at specific points within the authentication flow. A custom authentication extension is essentially an event listener that, when activated, makes an HTTP call to a REST API endpoint where you define a workflow action. For example, you could add an [attribute collection](#attribute-collection-start-and-submit-events) workflow to validate the attributes a user enters during sign-up, or you could use a [custom claims provider](#token-issuance-start-event) to add external user data to the token before the token is issued.
